messages.subject: Re: Stuck with FALSE command during installation of camtrapR Package
messages.subject_clean: Stuck with FALSE command during installation of camtrapR Package
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
R fails to install dependencies of camtrapR (other packages that camtrapR needs to run). Therefore you can't load camtrapR, even though it installed on your system.

Try installing the package with:

install.packages("camtrapR", dependencies = TRUE)

If that fails, try first:
install.packages("rotl", dependencies = TRUE)
install.packages("taxize", dependencies = TRUE)

Does that help?

Also, when asked this:

  There are binary versions available but the source versions are later:
       binary source needs_compilation
rotl    3.0.7  3.0.9             FALSE
taxize  0.9.6  0.9.8             FALSE

Does it ask you if you want to install from source? If is asks you, answer no. Install the binary, not source. Installing from source may fail if  there is source code (like C code) in the package which needs to be compiled.

And you may want to consider updating your R. Sometimes that solves problems. See the link for an easy way to update:
https://www.r-statistics.com/2013/03/updating-r-from-r-on-windows-using-the-installr-package/

Any luck with these suggestions?

messages.subject: Re: vignettes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Angela,
you can find the vignettes under this link:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/

Alternatively, run either of these:

vignette("ImageOrganisation", package = "camtrapR")
vignette("SpeciesIndividualIdentification", package = "camtrapR")
vignette("DataExtraction", package = "camtrapR")
vignette("DataExploration", package = "camtrapR")

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: camOp table construction
messages.body_plain: hello, how could you declare discontinuous periods of inactivity or inoperability of a camera? for the construction of a camOp table. I have 3 years of sampling only in the dry season. Thank you
messages.body_snippet: hello, how could you declare discontinuous periods of inactivity or inoperability of a camera? for the construction of a camOp table. I have 3 years of sampling only in the dry season. Thank you

messages.subject: Re: camOp table construction
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the next version will include a "sessionCol" argument in the function cameraOperation, but it is not out yet.

The best strategy until then depends on how your data were collected and what you are trying to do. Can you please share how your cameras were set up (i.e., multiple cameras per station?) and what analyses you wish to conduct?

Some ideas though. For each camera / station that was operated discontinuously, you could:

1) have multiple entries in the station column of your camera trap information table for the cameras
2) have multiple entries in the camera column of your camera trap information table (same station, different cameras)
3) have one entry in your camera trap information table per camera and use the "Problem1_from" / "Problem1_to" way of declaring periods on inactivity.

Let me know and I'll be able to answer more precisely.
Best,
Jürgen
